section_summary: This section traces the 1946 agreement to ship U.S. cotton to Japan, manufacture it into textiles, and use export proceeds to repay the cotton and shipping costs. It also records disputes over India's share of Japanese cotton imports, textile export markets, pricing, and 1947 procurement and financing. The final pages introduce proposed revisions to the agreement.

subfiles.title: Cotton shipment and textile repayment agreement
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Secretary of War; Chairman, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Sets terms for shipping CCC cotton to Japan and repaying costs from textile sales.
subfiles.summary: The agreement assigns cotton supply to CCC, transport and textile sales to USCC, and Japanese production supervision to SCAP. It defines pricing, title, security, accounting, insurance, proceeds, reporting, and termination. Page 7 carries a noisy acceptance or signature.

subfiles.title: Permanent file copy routing form
subfiles.about: Records internal handling of the preceding agreement.
subfiles.summary: Blank or nearly blank permanent file copy form.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to approve cotton arrangement
subfiles.about: Recommends approval of the Agriculture Department's cotton agreement.
subfiles.summary: Notes the program can revive Japanese industry without excluding other cotton suppliers.

subfiles.title: Instructions for signing agreement copies
subfiles.about: Explains the signatures needed on copies of Secretary Anderson's agreement.
subfiles.summary: Requests Clayton's signature on agreement copies and accompanying transmittal letters.

subfiles.title: Indian and American cotton supplies for Japan
subfiles.about: Urges equal access for Indian and American cotton in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Minor contrasts immediate equal imports with temporary U.S. exclusivity and argues that excluding India would harm trade principles and relations with India.

subfiles.title: War Department acceptance and delivery forms
subfiles.about: Accepts the cotton agreement and encloses delivery and title forms.
subfiles.summary: Accepts terms while disclaiming use of War Department appropriations for possible losses.

subfiles.title: Signed duplicate of cotton agreement
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Secretary of War; U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Duplicates the February 7 agreement for signature and filing.
subfiles.summary: This noisy copy repeats the interagency terms for CCC cotton shipments to Japan and repayment through exported textiles. It ends with an acceptance signature.

subfiles.title: Transfer of title to Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Provides a form to transfer Japanese merchandise to USCC.
subfiles.summary: Blank title transfer and SCAP endorsement for merchandise delivered to USCC.

subfiles.title: Receipt for cotton
subfiles.about: Provides a receipt and SCAP endorsement for imported cotton.
subfiles.summary: Blank bale receipt records cotton delivered by USCC on behalf of CCC.

subfiles.title: State Department approval of delivery forms
subfiles.about: Confirms no objection to cotton delivery and textile transfer forms.
subfiles.summary: States that the agreement accords with policy on Japanese textile reactivation.

subfiles.title: McClellan forwards cotton council telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards a telegram opposing Indian cotton participation.
subfiles.summary: McClellan endorses the attached writer's views and requests consideration.

subfiles.title: Sid Y. West telegram to McClellan
subfiles.about: Urges use of U.S. surplus cotton for Japan instead of Indian cotton.
subfiles.summary: West asks the senator to contact Byrnes and Anderson immediately.

subfiles.title: Reply to McClellan on cotton sources
subfiles.about: Explains how Japanese cotton imports will be allocated.
subfiles.summary: Initial U.S. cotton shipments will proceed; the Far Eastern Commission will address later supply.

subfiles.title: Fulbright forwards cotton council telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards Sid Y. West's objection to British and Indian cotton participation.
subfiles.summary: Fulbright highlights opposition to a proposed 40 percent Indian share.

subfiles.title: Sid Y. West telegram to Fulbright
subfiles.about: Asks Fulbright to defend a U.S. cotton supply plan for Japan.
subfiles.summary: West objects to a British backed Indian share and asks for immediate contacts with cabinet secretaries.

subfiles.title: Reply to Fulbright on cotton sources
subfiles.about: Explains India's historic share and planned Far Eastern Commission review.
subfiles.summary: Promises U.S. cotton for initial mill operations, with later sources to be determined.

subfiles.title: War Department confirmation of cotton contract
subfiles.about: Confirms War Department satisfaction with the interagency contract.
subfiles.summary: Reports signed copies dispatched on February 28.

subfiles.title: Agriculture reply on 1946 cotton shipments
subfiles.about: Discusses shipments and possible Indian supply for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports April shipments and questions whether Agriculture must supply 890,000 bales in 1946.

subfiles.title: War Department approval of interagency committee
subfiles.about: Approves representatives to coordinate the cotton contract.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Agriculture's proposal with War Department representatives named.

subfiles.title: Proposal for cotton agreement committee
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State and War; U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Proposes one representative and alternate from each agency.
subfiles.summary: The committee would coordinate operational decisions without changing the agreement.

subfiles.title: Indian cotton availability
subfiles.about: Relays India's assurance that it can supply cotton to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains that India's export ban was meant to restrain cloth prices; detailed stock figures were still being collected.

subfiles.title: Textile Export Association sales proposals
subfiles.about: Suggests markets, prices, and procedures for selling Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: The association prioritizes Asian markets and seeks protection for American textile exports.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Textile Export Association
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the association's textile distribution proposals.
subfiles.summary: Promises consideration of Murray's recommendations.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese textile distribution
subfiles.about: Explains constraints on sales of Japanese textiles.
subfiles.summary: Sales will reflect regional need, Allied decisions, and acceptable financial terms.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on reserving additional CCC cotton
subfiles.about: Supports reserving cotton beyond the original 650,000 bales.
subfiles.summary: Additional reserves could serve 1947 needs or cover a shortfall in Indian supply.

subfiles.title: Request to hold additional cotton
subfiles.about: Confirms an interagency understanding on continued cotton supply.
subfiles.summary: Requests that CCC preserve cotton for future Japanese shipments while potential alternative sources are assessed.

subfiles.title: Cotton pricing examples
subfiles.about: Calculates agreement prices for cotton grades shipped to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses June 19 spot quotations and shows FAS and Kobe CIF calculations.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning cotton quotations
subfiles.about: Discusses cotton price calculations and encloses a quotation sheet.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR preserves pricing figures and a cotton quotations enclosure.

subfiles.title: Reply to Japan Tea Committee
subfiles.about: Addresses cooperation on importing and distributing Japanese tea.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture will discuss the committee's tea import proposals; this appears misfiled in the cotton bundle.

subfiles.title: Textile exporters request consultation
subfiles.about: Requests textile exporters' views be heard before sales decisions.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Clayton for conveying the association's views to Allied committees.

subfiles.title: USCC transmits cotton pricing interpretation
subfiles.about: Sends signed copies of a supplementary cotton pricing interpretation.
subfiles.summary: Requests State Department approval and distribution of copies.

subfiles.title: Pricing Japanese cotton under agreement
subfiles.about: Defines the date used to price cotton shipped to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Uses the market price when USCC issues shipping instructions for a specified vessel.

subfiles.title: State approval of pricing interpretation
subfiles.about: Approves the supplementary Japanese cotton pricing agreement.
subfiles.summary: Retains the original and forwards signed copies to the other representatives.

subfiles.title: 1946–47 Japanese cotton import memorandum transmittal
subfiles.about: Sends a summary of Japan's 1946 and 1947 cotton import programs.
subfiles.summary: Asks Badger to circulate copies to the Inter-Allied Trade Board.

subfiles.title: Supplement to proposed follow-up cotton program
subfiles.about: Sends revised 1947 cotton arrival and revolving fund estimates.
subfiles.summary: Revises the plan because expected American cotton consumption in Japan had fallen.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Hynds supplement
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the revised cotton program supplement.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Hynds for sending copies to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese yarn for Middle East territories
subfiles.about: Supports prompt purchase talks for Japanese yarn needed in the Middle East.
subfiles.summary: States that USCC may offer yarn broadly after March 1 and that supply appears adequate.

subfiles.title: Classification check on yarn letter
subfiles.about: Questions the security classification of an enclosure.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten reply says British board members already receive the paper.

subfiles.title: British request for Japanese cotton yarn
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese yarn supplies for Aden, Eritrea, and Tripolitania.
subfiles.summary: Reports shortages after India suspended yarn exports and asks whether Japanese supply can open.

subfiles.title: Request for urgent Gearhart reply
subfiles.about: Requests a prompt reply to Representative Gearhart.
subfiles.summary: Seeks a draft for Acheson's signature by April 24.

subfiles.title: Gearhart inquiry on foreign cotton financing
subfiles.about: Asks whether U.S. agencies will finance foreign cotton for Japan and Germany.
subfiles.summary: Cites concern among San Joaquin Valley cotton growers and asks for an urgent account of any plans.

subfiles.title: Meeting with Senator Eastland on cotton procurement
subfiles.about: Reports senators' objections to the proposed Japanese cotton procurement mix.
subfiles.summary: The senators wanted a longer program and assurance that U.S. cotton would replace unavailable Indian cotton.

subfiles.title: Cotton bloc meeting
subfiles.about: Reports congressional demands for U.S. cotton shares in Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Eastland requests historic market shares and a full procurement program through 1947.

subfiles.title: Congressional pressure and foreign cotton supply
subfiles.about: Explains procurement pressure and possible Indian, Brazilian, and Egyptian supply.
subfiles.summary: Warns that heavy U.S. purchases could raise domestic prices and urges a clear government policy.

subfiles.title: Foreign cotton availability
subfiles.about: Estimates cotton exports available from Brazil, Egypt, India, and Peru.
subfiles.summary: Lists prospective volumes and India's proposed 394,000-bale SCAP program.

subfiles.title: Additional foreign cotton availability note
subfiles.about: Summarizes projected foreign cotton availability and prices.
subfiles.summary: Noisy note repeats Brazilian, Egyptian, Indian, and Peruvian export estimates.

subfiles.title: Proposed Export-Import Bank loan to joint agency
subfiles.about: Reviews financing discussions for German raw material imports.
subfiles.summary: Claxton recounts talks with private banks and the Export-Import Bank about credit secured by a Bizonal Agency fund. He urges senior officials to approach the bank's board directly.

subfiles.title: Meeting with Export-Import Bank chairman
subfiles.about: Recommends senior discussion of German trade financing with Mr. Martin.
subfiles.summary: Describes a possible $20 million credit line against a $5 million agency pledge.

subfiles.title: Review of Lamar Fleming's occupied areas cotton plan
subfiles.about: Evaluates a private textile bank proposal for supplying cotton to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The review rejects private credit decisions for individual Japanese mills during occupation. It favors centralized procurement and finds the proposal unclear about financing risks and converting textiles into dollars.

subfiles.title: Additional signed copies of revised cotton agreement
subfiles.about: Requests signed copies of the July 1947 cotton agreement amendments.
subfiles.summary: One copy would go to USCC and one remain with the Secretary.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on revised U.S. cotton agreement
subfiles.about: Recommends accepting amendments to the cotton supply agreement.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the revisions and related British proposal for Japan–Sterling Area trade; the memorandum continues beyond this section.
